papers.title: Codeveloping a Clinical Pathway for Recurrent Clostridioides difficile Infection With Primary Care Providers: User-Centered Design Study.
papers.abstract: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is the most common cause of health care-associated infectious diarrhea; however, variability in laboratory testing results in uncertainty in diagnosis and clinical decision-making. Recurrent CDI (rCDI), defined as the return of infection following initial treatment, continues to present significant clinical challenges due to limited therapeutic options. Although health care providers are familiar with vancomycin as first-line therapy for CDI, many are less familiar with fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), despite its recommendation in clinical guide
papers.summary: This study used user-centered design to develop a clinical pathway for managing recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection (rCDI) in collaboration with primary care providers. The work addresses diagnostic uncertainty from variable laboratory testing and limited provider familiarity with fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) despite guideline recommendations. The resulting pathway aims to standardize and improve rCDI management in primary care settings.

papers.title: Butyrate Triggers Neuronal Signaling via Release of Colonic Serotonin in a Microfluidic Model of Gut-Brain Axis.
papers.abstract: Host-microbiota interactions play a central role in regulating gastrointestinal and cardiometabolic physiology, yet the mechanistic pathways linking microbial metabolites to sensory neuronal activation remain poorly defined. In particular, the rapid signaling events through which short-chain fatty acids such as butyrate influence epithelial and neuronal function in the colon have not been fully resolved due to limitations of existing models. Here, we developed and validated a compartmentalized microfluidic tri-channel model that spatially organizes primary colonic epithelial cells, sensory neu
papers.journal: American journal of physiology. Gastrointestinal and liver physiology
papers.summary: Researchers developed a compartmentalized microfluidic tri-channel model that co-cultures primary colonic epithelial cells and sensory neurons to study gut-brain signaling. Using this system, they found that the microbial metabolite butyrate triggers neuronal signaling indirectly by stimulating colonic epithelial cells to release serotonin. This provides a mechanistic link between short-chain fatty acids and sensory neuronal activation in the colon.

papers.title: Design and evaluation of a streamlined enrichment method for faster co-detection of enteric bacterial pathogens in natural soils and environmental samples.
papers.abstract: This study developed a streamlined, sensitive and rapid method for co-detection of low concentrations of Salmonella enterica, Shigella flexneri, Listeria monocytogenes, and pathogenic Escherichia coli from soil. First, autoclaved soil from Iowa with serial dilutions of bacteria to confirm individual species recovery rates on selective agar by qPCR under varying primary enrichment times was used. All pathogens were detected by qPCR of colonies recovered from replicate sterile soils spiked with 10^1 or greater bacteria within 5 hours of enrichment. Shiga toxin expressing E. coli (STEC) and L. mo
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This study presents a streamlined enrichment protocol that enables simultaneous detection of four enteric bacterial pathogens (Salmonella, Shigella, Listeria, and pathogenic E. coli) from soil samples within 5 hours. The method combines primary enrichment with selective agar plating and qPCR, achieving detection of bacteria at concentrations as low as 10^1 CFU from spiked sterile soils. This approach addresses the need for rapid, sensitive co-detection of multiple pathogens in environmental samples.

papers.title: Microbes on the Mind: Multi-modal Neuroimaging Reveals Gut-Brain Axes in Infants.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiome undergoes rapid maturation after birth and has been associated with cognition and mental health, yet its relation to early brain development remains poorly defined. We analyzed 223 typically developing children aged 0-3 years with multimodal MRI and paired fecal shotgun metagenomics. Microbiome-wide association analyses identified associations with cortical morphology, white-matter microstructure, and functional connectivity. Ridge-regularized canonical correlation analysis identified two principal covariance patterns: a structural-metabolic mode and a functional-taxonomic m
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study paired fecal metagenomics with multimodal MRI in 223 typically developing children aged 0-3 years to test whether gut microbiome composition relates to early brain development. Microbiome-wide association analyses linked microbial features to cortical morphology, white-matter microstructure, and functional connectivity, and canonical correlation analysis revealed two main covariance patterns: a structural-metabolic mode and a functional-taxonomic mode. The findings suggest that gut-brain axes are detectable very early in life, though the cross-sectional design limits causal inference.

papers.title: Lossless compression of protein databases for efficient and accurate metagenomic sequence classification with Centrifuger.
papers.abstract: We present a lossless compression algorithm for indexing a protein database while supporting fast taxonomic classification in the method Centrifuger. The algorithm is a new scheme of the previously proposed run-block compression algorithm to reduce the size of the Ferragina-Manzini (FM) index, and it scales better with alphabet size than the original. On the RefSeq prokaryotic and viral protein sequences, Centrifuger reduces the memory footprint by over a third compared to the method Kaiju that builds on a plain FM-index, while having comparable running time. Furthermore, the compressed FM-ind
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Centrifuger introduces a lossless compression algorithm for indexing protein databases that reduces the memory footprint of the Ferragina-Manzini index by over a third compared to Kaiju while maintaining comparable speed. This enables efficient and accurate taxonomic classification of metagenomic sequences against large reference protein databases.

papers.title: Improving Metagenomics Classification with Kmask: Entropy-Based Masking of Low-Complexity Regions.
papers.abstract: Accurate taxonomic classification in metagenomics is often compromised by low-complexity sequences, which lead to chance matches that in turn cause sequences to be misclassified. Here we present Kmask, an entropy-based masking tool implemented for use either standalone or as part of Kraken [1,2] database construction, which replaces low-entropy regions with Ns. Using a sliding window size aligned with Kraken's default k-mer length and parameters optimized across 12 control bacterial genomes spanning a broad range of GC content, Kmask efficiently removes low-complexity sequences while retaining
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Kmask is a new entropy-based masking tool that replaces low-complexity regions in metagenomic sequences with Ns to reduce spurious matches during taxonomic classification. It can be used standalone or integrated into Kraken database construction, with parameters optimized across 12 bacterial genomes with varying GC content. The tool aims to improve classification accuracy by removing low-complexity sequences that often cause misclassification.

papers.title: Microbial transmission and ecology of human and environmental microbial communities in childcare centers.
papers.abstract: Background Early-life microbial exposures profoundly impact lifelong health trajectories by shaping immune maturation and modulating disease risk, e.g. as described by the "hygiene hypothesis." Childcare facilities represent a critical yet understudied source of microbial exposures where preschool-aged children spend 7-10 hours daily during key developmental periods. This study presents the first multi-omic and multi-kingdom investigation of microbial transmission and community ecology across childcare environments, integrating microbiome samples from both high-touch and low-touch surfaces wit
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omic and multi-kingdom profiling to characterize microbial communities and transmission patterns across childcare center environments, sampling both high-touch and low-touch surfaces alongside human-associated microbes. It represents the first comprehensive investigation of how microbes move between children, staff, and surfaces in these settings, with implications for early-life immune exposure and the hygiene hypothesis.

papers.title: Sequencing the wastewater virome: Current strategies and bioinformatic pitfalls.
papers.abstract: Wastewater-based surveillance (WBS) is a powerful tool for monitoring viral pathogens at the population level, complementing clinical surveillance through anonymous and unbiased insights into viral circulation. Wastewater sequencing allows to move beyond detection toward detailed characterization of circulating pathogens. This review outlines the two main sequencing strategies used in WBS: targeted and untargeted approaches. Targeted methods, including amplicon- and probe-based sequencing, provide sensitive detection and recovery of known viruses but are limited in identifying novel pathogens.
papers.summary: This review compares targeted (amplicon- and probe-based) and untargeted sequencing strategies for wastewater-based surveillance of viral pathogens, highlighting trade-offs between sensitivity for known viruses and the ability to detect novel ones. It also catalogs common bioinformatic pitfalls in wastewater virome analysis, offering guidance for more reliable population-level viral monitoring.

papers.title: Deciphering the heterogeneity of prodromal α-synucleinopathy: linking brain biotyping and gut dysbiosis in isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder.
papers.abstract: Isolated/idiopathic REM sleep behaviour disorder (iRBD) is a specific prodrome of α-synucleinopathies. We previously identified two distinct clinical-neuroimaging biotypes in iRBD: Biotype 1, marked by widespread cortical-subcortical-cerebellar atrophy with motor and cognitive deficits, and Biotype 2, with preserved brain structure and neurocognition. Converging evidence implicates the gut-brain axis in early α-synucleinopathy, yet its role in these divergent iRBD phenotypes remains unexplored.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether the two previously identified brain biotypes of isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder (iRBD) — one with widespread brain atrophy and cognitive/motor deficits, the other with preserved brain structure — differ in their gut microbiome composition. By linking brain biotyping with gut dysbiosis, the authors aim to clarify how gut-brain axis alterations relate to divergent prodromal α-synucleinopathy phenotypes. The findings could help stratify iRBD patients by underlying disease trajectory.

papers.title: Integrated multi-omics and metabolic modeling links structure to function in high-performing electrosynthetic biofilm communities.
papers.abstract: Microbial electrosynthesis (MES) is a promising technology for the valorization of CO2 into industrially relevant building blocks. The high-performing MES systems in terms of production rates of acetate (12.5-19.7 mmol L-1catholyte day-1), butyrate (1.9-12.2 mmol L-1catholyte day-1), and caproate (0.6-0.9 mmol L-1catholyte day-1) discussed in this study consist of mixed microbial communities. However, the microbial community members, metabolic pathways, and interactions driving product formation in MES communities remain poorly understood. To overcome these challenges, we conducted a comprehen
papers.summary: This study combines multi-omics profiling with metabolic modeling to characterize the microbial community members, pathways, and interactions driving high-rate production of acetate, butyrate, and caproate in electrosynthetic biofilms. The integrated approach links community structure to metabolic function, revealing how mixed microbial consortia convert CO2 into valuable chemical building blocks in microbial electrosynthesis systems.

papers.title: Novel Antarctic chemolithotroph drives iron biomineralization.
papers.abstract: Iron, the most abundant redox-active metal in the Earth's crust, is coupled to numerous biogeochemical cycles. However, the mechanisms of iron oxidation and the organisms involved remain incompletely understood. Banded iron formations (BIFs) are a major reservoir of iron ore in the Precambrian sedimentary record, yet the biological contribution to their genesis remains a subject of unresolved debate. While large-scale BIF deposition largely ceased after the Proterozoic, microbial activity in modern Holocene sediments under fluctuating redox conditions provides a unique opportunity to examine m
papers.summary: This study characterizes a novel chemolithotrophic microorganism from Antarctic sediments that oxidizes iron and drives biomineralization. The finding provides a modern analog for understanding the biological mechanisms potentially involved in the formation of ancient banded iron formations (BIFs). It expands knowledge of microbial iron cycling under fluctuating redox conditions in extreme environments.

papers.title: [Translated article] The "Trojan horse" against antimicrobial resistance: Siderophore conjugates and public health.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance, particularly in carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales such as KPC-type, represents a critical threat to public health in Latin America, associated with high mortality rates and increased healthcare costs. This systematic review aims to evaluate the therapeutic potential of siderophore-drug and siderophore-peptide conjugates against priority multidrug-resistant pathogens, including Enterobacterales, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Acinetobacter baumannii, analyzing their efficacy, mechanisms of action, and implementation challenges.
papers.journal: Farmacia hospitalaria : organo oficial de expresion cientifica de la Sociedad Espanola de Farmacia Hospitalaria
papers.summary: This systematic review examines siderophore-drug and siderophore-peptide conjugates as a strategy to combat multidrug-resistant pathogens like carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Acinetobacter baumannii. These 'Trojan horse' molecules exploit bacterial iron-uptake systems to deliver antimicrobials directly into resistant bacteria, potentially overcoming existing resistance mechanisms. The review analyzes their efficacy, mechanisms of action, and barriers to clinical implementation.

papers.title: Escherichia coli-derived enterobactin is associated with delayed gut microbiome maturation in infants born to mothers with obesity.
papers.abstract: Maternal obesity has been increasingly recognized as a factor influencing early-life microbiome development. However, its impact on the infant gut resistome and virulome remains insufficiently characterized. In this prospective longitudinal study, we investigated gut microbiome composition, antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), and virulence factor profiles in infants born to mothers with obesity and normal weight during the first year of life. Shotgun metagenomic sequencing was performed on maternal and infant fecal samples collected at birth and at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months. Infants born to obese
papers.summary: This prospective longitudinal study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to track gut microbiome composition, antibiotic resistance genes, and virulence factors in infants born to mothers with obesity versus normal weight over the first year of life. The key finding is that Escherichia coli-derived enterobactin is associated with delayed gut microbiome maturation in infants of mothers with obesity, linking maternal obesity to altered early-life microbiome development and resistome/virulome profiles.

papers.title: A joint mixture Tobit method with latent microbial abundance improves detection of microbiome-disease associations in zero-inflated data.
papers.abstract: Zero inflation remains a major challenge in microbiome differential abundance analysis, often resulting in inflated type I error rates or reduced statistical power. Although numerous methods have been proposed to address excess zeros, many existing approaches do not explicitly distinguish between distinct zero-generating mechanisms, and censoring-based modeling perspectives remain relatively underexplored in microbiome data analysis. To advance methodological development in this area, we introduce a novel censoring-based modeling perspective for microbiome differential abundance analysis. Spec
papers.summary: The paper introduces a joint mixture Tobit model that treats zero-inflated microbiome counts as censored observations of a latent microbial abundance, explicitly distinguishing between structural and sampling zeros. This censoring-based framework improves statistical power and controls type I error in detecting microbiome-disease associations compared to existing differential abundance methods.

papers.title: Peripheral microbial metabolites as indicators of gut microbiome disruption: systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Gut microbiome disruption is often characterized by the loss of obligately anaerobic bacteria, which may lead to altered production of microbial metabolites that can be detected peripherally. The application of widely used sequencing-based microbiome analyses to clinical settings is limited by cost, turnaround time, and challenges with patients with very low stool output. Since some products of strictly bacterial metabolism are detectable in blood, peripheral metabolites may provide a rapid and scalable indicator of gut microbiome composition and function. We performed a systematic review and
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis examines whether microbial metabolites detectable in peripheral blood can serve as indicators of gut microbiome disruption, particularly the loss of obligately anaerobic bacteria. The authors argue that such metabolites could offer a faster, cheaper, and more scalable alternative to sequencing-based microbiome analysis in clinical settings, especially for patients with low stool output.

papers.title: Mallard super-shedders of avian influenza exhibit distinct cloacal microbial abundance profiles.
papers.abstract: In many infectious disease systems, a small fraction of hosts accounts for a disproportionate share of transmission, but the biological basis of this heterogeneity remains poorly resolved. In avian influenza, mallards show substantial variation in viral shedding, raising the possibility that only a subset of individuals contributes strongly to environmental contamination and onward spread. To examine whether host microbiome structure is associated with this variation, we experimentally infected wild, captive mallards with low-pathogenic avian influenza virus. We characterized cloacal microbiom
papers.summary: This study experimentally infected captive wild mallards with low-pathogenic avian influenza and found that individuals with the highest viral shedding ('super-shedders') had distinct cloacal microbiome abundance profiles compared to low-shedding birds. The results suggest that host microbiome composition may contribute to heterogeneity in influenza transmission.

papers.title: Chestnut-quebracho tannins shape the fecal metabolome of weaned pigs through microbiota-dependent urolithin production.
papers.abstract: Chestnut and quebracho tannins may support gut health in weaned piglets, but their efficacy likely depends on farm environment and microbial capacity to convert tannins into bioactive metabolites. This study evaluated the effects of a blend of chestnut-derived hydrolysable tannins and quebracho-derived condensed tannins on growth performance, diarrhea occurrence, gut metagenome, and fecal metabolome in piglets reared under two commercial farm conditions. A total of 160 weaned piglets (initial body weight 6.53 ± 0.13 kg) were assigned to a 2 × 2 factorial design comprising 2 weaning units (W1 a
papers.journal: Journal of animal science and biotechnology
papers.summary: This study investigated how a blend of chestnut (hydrolysable) and quebracho (condensed) tannins affects weaned piglets raised under two different commercial farm conditions. The researchers found that the tannins' effects on growth, diarrhea, gut metagenome, and fecal metabolome depended on the farm environment and the gut microbiota's ability to convert tannins into bioactive urolithin metabolites. This highlights that tannin supplementation efficacy is microbiota- and context-dependent.

papers.title: Biosynthetic origin of anticancer dolastatin 15 reveals a noncanonical NRPS architecture enabling 2-keto acid activation.
papers.abstract: Elucidating the biological origins and biosynthetic pathways of marine natural products remains a major challenge, particularly for compounds derived from microbial consortia. Here, we identify the marine cyanobacterial genus Dapis as the source of the potent anticancer natural product dolastatin 15 using genome-resolved metagenomics. Reconstruction of two complete and two near-complete genomes provides genome-resolved characterization of the genus Dapis, revealing extensive biosynthetic potential. Genome mining identified the dolastatin 15 biosynthetic gene cluster. Subsequent analyses recons
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.summary: Using genome-resolved metagenomics, the authors identified the marine cyanobacterial genus Dapis as the biological source of the anticancer compound dolastatin 15. They discovered its biosynthetic gene cluster and revealed a noncanonical NRPS architecture that enables activation of 2-keto acids, expanding understanding of how these complex molecules are made.

papers.title: Network-guided synthesis of antagonistic microbiota for suppressing maize stalk rot disease.
papers.abstract: Plant-associated microbiomes play a crucial role in sustaining host health and fitness, but how pathogen invasion reshapes microbial interaction networks and how to leverage this for developing effective biocontrol strategies remain poorly understood. This study investigated the maize microbiome under Fusarium stalk rot stress by integrating large-scale amplicon sequencing, network refinement, and experimental validation. To distinguish biological interactions from spurious associations driven by environmental and geographic factors, we applied a refined analytical framework to filter out abio
papers.summary: This study used large-scale amplicon sequencing and network refinement to map how Fusarium stalk rot infection reshapes the maize microbiome, filtering out environmental and geographic artifacts to identify genuine microbial interactions. The authors then synthesized antagonistic microbial consortia guided by these networks and experimentally validated their ability to suppress maize stalk rot disease.

papers.title: Leviathan: fast, memory-efficient, and scalable taxonomic and pathway profiling for (pan)genome-resolved metagenomics and metatranscriptomics.
papers.abstract: Functional profiling of meta-omics is essential for understanding microbial communities, yet support for custom genome-resolved reference databases is limited. We introduce Leviathan for integrated taxonomic and functional profiling at both genome and pangenome resolution. Leviathan combines Sylph for ultrafast alignment-free taxonomic profiling with Salmon for pseudo-alignment-based read quantification in DNA space against (pan)genome-resolved gene catalogs, producing dual metrics per (pan)genome: pathway abundance and graph-based pathway coverage. Benchmarking alignment backends on synthetic
papers.summary: Leviathan is a new tool that combines fast alignment-free taxonomic profiling (Sylph) with pseudo-alignment-based gene quantification (Salmon) to enable integrated taxonomic and functional profiling of metagenomes and metatranscriptomes against custom genome- and pangenome-resolved reference databases. It outputs both pathway abundance and graph-based pathway coverage per genome, addressing the limited support for custom reference databases in existing functional profiling tools.

papers.title: PanGBank: a large-scale resource of precomputed microbial pangenomes built with PPanGGOLiN.
papers.abstract: PanGBank (https://pangbank.genoscope.cns.fr) is a comprehensive open-access database providing precomputed prokaryotic pangenomes at a broad taxonomic scale. Built upon PPanGGOLiN partitioned pangenome graphs, PanGBank addresses the growing need for large-scale comparative genomics through a standardized, regularly updated, and fully accessible resource. The initial release comprises two complementary collections covering >4600 prokaryotic species from the Genome Taxonomy Database (GTDB), encompassing over 393 000 genomes: GTDB_all, maximizing taxonomic and environmental diversity through the
papers.summary: PanGBank is a new open-access database that provides precomputed pangenomes for over 4,600 prokaryotic species (more than 393,000 genomes), built using the PPanGGOLiN partitioned pangenome graph method. It offers a standardized, regularly updated resource for large-scale comparative genomics, removing the computational burden of generating pangenomes from scratch.

papers.title: Metagenomic analysis of rhizosphere soil microbiota in wild and cultivated Notopterygium incisum, an umbelliferae medicinal herb.
papers.abstract: Notopterygium incisum is not only a traditional Chinese medicine but also an endemic herb. Artificial domestication and large-scale cultivation are crucial for resolving the crisis of wild resources and the supply-demand imbalance of N. incisum, yet current techniques have failed to stably provide the herb medicine in good quality. Metagenomic analyses revealed significant differences in the rhizomicrobiota between wild and cultivated N. incisum, particularly in microbial composition, gene functions, and community assembly. The rhizomicrobiota of the wild N. incisum from 3 different sites with
papers.summary: This study used metagenomic sequencing to compare the rhizosphere soil microbiota of wild versus cultivated Notopterygium incisum, a traditional Chinese medicinal herb. The authors found significant differences in microbial composition, gene functions, and community assembly between wild and cultivated plants across multiple sites. These findings suggest that domestication and cultivation practices alter the root-associated microbiome, which may help explain quality inconsistencies in cultivated herbs.

papers.title: How safe from Listeria monocytogenes are frozen ready-to-eat fish products, either cooked or smoked, when stored under refrigeration after purchasing?
papers.abstract: This research aimed to access the incidence of Listeria sp. and L. monocytogenes in frozen ready-to-eat (RTE) fish products immediately after purchasing, and after refrigerated storage. Out of 72 kani-kama samples, 17 (23,6%) and 16 out of 48 samples (33,3%) of smoked salmon samples, tested positive for Listeria sp. by the traditional culture method, whereas 45,8% and 56.2% were positive by PCR, for kani-kama and smoked salmon samples, respectively. Applying qPCR, 21 samples of kani-kama out of 72 (29.2%) and 23 out of 48 samples of smoked and sliced salmon (47.9%) were positive for L. monocyt
papers.journal: Brazilian journal of microbiology : [publication of the Brazilian Society for Microbiology]
papers.summary: This study tested frozen ready-to-eat fish products (kani-kama and smoked salmon) for Listeria contamination immediately after purchase and after refrigerated storage. Using culture, PCR, and qPCR, they found Listeria in a substantial fraction of samples, with smoked salmon showing higher contamination rates than kani-kama. The findings highlight potential food safety risks from these products even when kept refrigerated.

papers.title: Comparative evaluation of methods for measuring standardized ileal digestibility of amino acids for different sorghum varieties in broilers.
papers.abstract: This study investigated the effects of two evaluation methods (direct vs. substitution) on standardized ileal amino acid digestibility (SIDAA) and intestinal digestive physiology in broilers fed sorghum from six regional sources. There were 336 27-d-old Cobb broilers assigned to 14 treatments, including a nitrogen-free diet (NFD), a corn-soybean meal (CSM) basal diet, and 12 experimental diets arranged in a 2 × 6 factorial arrangement. In the direct method, sorghum served as the only source of dietary amino acids whereas in substitution method the test sorghum replaced 40% (w/w) of the basal d
papers.summary: This study compared direct and substitution methods for measuring standardized ileal amino acid digestibility (SIDAA) in broilers fed sorghum from six regional sources. Using 336 broilers across 14 dietary treatments, the authors assessed how the two evaluation methods affect digestibility estimates and intestinal digestive physiology. The findings highlight methodological differences that could influence how sorghum varieties are assessed for poultry feed formulation.

papers.title: Salivary microbiome responses to chlorhexidine and Coriandrum sativum essential oil mouthwashes in patients with periodontitis in a randomized 2-week clinical trial.
papers.abstract: To compare the short-term salivary microbiome effects of a Coriandrum sativum essential oil (CSEO) mouthwash, chlorhexidine (CHX) as a benchmark comparator, and water in patients with periodontitis.
papers.summary: This randomized 2-week clinical trial compared the effects of a Coriandrum sativum essential oil mouthwash, chlorhexidine, and water on the salivary microbiome in periodontitis patients. The study characterizes how these mouthwashes shift bacterial community composition, providing short-term evidence on the microbiome impact of a natural alternative to chlorhexidine.

papers.title: A cross-families evaluation of using fecal samples as a method to study the amphibian gut microbiome.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota plays an important role in animals. Fecal samples are often used to study the gut microbiota because they are convenient to collect, allow for longitudinal sampling, and often necessary when studying rare and endangered species. In this study, we evaluate the effectiveness of using fecal samples by characterizing and comparing the microbiota of feces and the gut (small intestine mucosa, large intestine mucosa) for representatives of seven amphibian families. This includes the first data from a salamander species. Additionally, we compared fecal samples before (pre-feces) and
papers.summary: This study evaluates whether fecal samples accurately represent the gut microbiome across seven amphibian families, including the first such data from a salamander. By comparing microbial communities in feces versus small and large intestine mucosa, the authors assess the reliability of non-invasive fecal sampling for studying amphibian gut microbiota.

papers.title: Microbial community composition on polytetrafluoroethylene tape retrieved from implant screw channels: A cross-sectional high-throughput 16S rRNA sequencing study.
papers.abstract: To identify the types of microorganisms colonizing the surface of polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) tape used for sealing the central screw channel in implant prostheses and to evaluate their association with the duration of prosthetic functional loading.
papers.journal: Infection, genetics and evolution : journal of molecular epidemiology and evolutionary genetics in infectious diseases
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study used high-throughput 16S rRNA sequencing to identify bacteria colonizing PTFE tape used to seal the central screw channel in implant prostheses, and assessed whether microbial composition relates to how long the prosthesis has been in function. The work characterizes the microbial community on this clinically relevant surface, providing a baseline for understanding biofilm formation in dental implant systems.

papers.title: Association of microbial pathways predicted/inferred using 16S and shotgun metagenome with faecal metabolite abundances.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiome is an essential metabolic organ influencing host health through metabolite production. While metabolite production levels can be directly measured by gas or liquid chromatography, they are commonly inferred from the abundance of metagenomic functional pathways. To evaluate the accuracy of these inferences, we established a single, manually curated metabolite-pathway/enzyme mapping list as a standardized biological reference. We then compared liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS)-based faecal metabolites with functional pathways/enzymes inferred from four approaches
papers.summary: This study evaluates how accurately gut microbial metabolite production can be inferred from metagenomic functional pathways by comparing LC-MS-measured faecal metabolites against pathways/enzymes predicted from 16S and shotgun metagenomes using four different inference approaches. The authors created a manually curated metabolite-pathway/enzyme mapping list as a standardized reference to benchmark these predictions. The work highlights the limitations and variability of inferring metabolite abundances from metagenomic data alone.

papers.title: Targeted genome recovery of under-sequenced microbes from the Sequence Read Archive STAT.
papers.abstract: Most microbial species are represented by a single genome in public databases. The lack of genomes for these 'singleton' organisms limits our understanding of their pan-genome diversity and evolution. Although the Sequence Read Archive (SRA) contains millions of sequencing datasets that could be used to expand our understanding of many species, the extent to which under-represented microbial species are present at levels sufficient for genome recovery is unclear. Here, we show that the pre-computed taxonomic profiles generated by the National Center for Biotechnology Information SRA Taxonomy A
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that the Sequence Read Archive contains enough sequencing data to recover genomes for many microbial species that currently have only a single representative genome in public databases. By leveraging pre-computed taxonomic profiles from NCBI's SRA Taxonomy Analysis Tool, the authors identify under-sequenced microbes and show that targeted genome recovery from existing metagenomic datasets is feasible. This approach can expand pan-genome diversity and improve understanding of microbial evolution without requiring new sequencing efforts.

papers.title: Deep-sea Microbial Dataset of the Antarctic Ocean (dsMDAO): A high-resolution deep-sea microbial dataset of the Antarctic Ocean reveals potential for taxonomic and functional diversity.
papers.abstract: Antarctic deep-sea ecosystems harboured unique and metabolically versatile micro-organisms that sustained key biogeochemical processes under extreme polar conditions. However, the genomic diversity and ecological functions of these sedimentary or deep-sea microbial communities remained largely unexplored. Here, we constructed a comprehensive deep-sea microbial dataset of the Antarctic Ocean (dsMDAO) by integrating three newly sequenced Prydz Bay sediment metagenomes with 22 publicly available datasets (9 seawater and 13 sediment samples), spanning water depths of ~300-3500 m. Genome binning yi
papers.summary: This study presents dsMDAO, a high-resolution metagenomic dataset of Antarctic deep-sea microbial communities built by combining three newly sequenced Prydz Bay sediment metagenomes with 22 public datasets spanning ~300-3500 m depths. Genome binning recovered microbial genomes that reveal substantial taxonomic and functional diversity, highlighting the metabolic versatility of polar deep-sea microorganisms. The resource provides a foundation for exploring biogeochemical roles of these understudied communities.

papers.title: Metagenomic Characterisation of Antibiotic Resistance in Anaerobic Digesters and Their Implications for Environmental Health.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in environmental systems represents an emerging One Health challenge, with anaerobic digesters potentially serving as reservoirs of resistance-associated genetic features. This study analysed four publicly available anaerobic digester shotgun metagenomic datasets (M2, M3, M12 and M17) retrieved from the NCBI Sequence Read Archive to characterise microbial functions, resistance-associated annotations and antibiotic target loci. The datasets were generated using Illumina HiSeq 2000 sequencing and analysed through quality assessment, assembly, functional annotation
papers.summary: This study reanalyzed four publicly available shotgun metagenomic datasets from anaerobic digesters to characterize microbial functions, antibiotic resistance genes, and antibiotic target loci. The findings suggest that anaerobic digesters may act as reservoirs of antimicrobial resistance determinants, with implications for environmental and One Health surveillance.

papers.title: Structural and Functional Characterisation of a Metagenome-Derived CYP108D18 Reveals an Unusual Dioxygen-Bound State and Selective Hydrocarbon Hydroxylation.
papers.abstract: Cytochrome P450 enzymes form a large superfamily of monooxygenases capable of oxidising diverse substrates. Among them, members of the CYP108 family are recognised for their role in monoterpenoid oxidation. In this study, we report the identification and characterisation of a new CYP108 family member, CYP108D18, from a metagenome-assembled genome derived from microbial communities in a geothermal hot spring located in northern Queensland, Australia. Taxonomic binning associated CYP108D18 with a Novosphingobium species, a genus well-known for its bioremediation potential. CYP108D18 was heterolo
papers.summary: Researchers identified and characterized a new cytochrome P450 enzyme, CYP108D18, from a metagenome-assembled genome of a geothermal hot spring microbial community, linking it to a Novosphingobium species. The enzyme displays an unusual dioxygen-bound state and selectively hydroxylates hydrocarbons, expanding knowledge of CYP108 family function beyond monoterpenoid oxidation.

papers.title: Exploring Blastocystis: hidden complexity in a common intestinal microbe.
papers.abstract: Blastocystis is an anaerobic stramenopile that colonizes the large intestine of humans and many animals worldwide. Small-subunit rRNA-based typing reveals deep genetic diversity: at least 44 genetic variants, namely, subtypes (STs), are recognized, with ST1-ST4 accounting for most human carriage. Its medical relevance remains contested. Blastocystis carriage is frequently asymptomatic, and while associations with non-specific gastrointestinal symptoms (e.g. diarrhoea, abdominal pain and bloating), irritable bowel syndrome and extraintestinal manifestations such as urticaria have been proposed.
papers.summary: This review examines Blastocystis, a common anaerobic gut microbe found in humans and animals worldwide, highlighting its extensive genetic diversity with at least 44 recognized subtypes. Despite its frequent presence in the human gut, whether Blastocystis causes disease remains controversial, as carriage is often asymptomatic but has been linked to gastrointestinal symptoms and conditions like IBS and urticaria.

papers.title: Evaluation of fecal microbiota, live (RBL) for the prevention of recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection: Canadian subgroup analysis of an open-label phase 3 study.
papers.abstract: Fecal microbiota, live (RBL) is a single-dose, broad consortium, microbiota-based product approved in the United States and Canada for preventing recurrent Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) infection in adults following standard-of-care (SOC) treatment.
papers.journal: Journal of the Canadian Association of Gastroenterology
papers.summary: This Canadian subgroup analysis of an open-label phase 3 trial evaluates fecal microbiota, live (RBL), a single-dose microbiota-based product, for preventing recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection after standard-of-care treatment. The findings support its use in the Canadian population, consistent with its approved indication in the US and Canada.

papers.title: LGTM: Gaussian process modulated neural topic modeling for longitudinal microbiome.
papers.abstract: Longitudinal microbiome data are key to understanding the dynamics of microbial communities and their relationships with the host and environment. However, analysis of such data is challenging due to high dimensionality, compositionality, irregular sampling and temporal dependencies on external covariates. Existing analytical approaches typically address only subsets of these challenges, limiting their ability to yield biologically interpretable insights. We introduce LGTM, a probabilistic modeling framework that combines flexible non-linear longitudinal modeling with interpretable topic-based
papers.summary: LGTM is a new probabilistic framework that combines Gaussian process-based longitudinal modeling with neural topic modeling to analyze longitudinal microbiome data. It addresses key challenges like high dimensionality, compositionality, irregular sampling, and temporal dependencies on external covariates, aiming to produce biologically interpretable insights into microbial community dynamics.

papers.title: From predicted bacteriocins to ecological function.
papers.abstract: Genome and metagenome mining have uncovered large repertoires of predicted bacteriocin loci, but ecological interpretation has lagged behind discovery. This review uses bacteriocins as a focused model for a broader problem in antimicrobial gene prediction: sequence identifies encoded potential, but it does not establish expression, product deployment, target engagement, or community-level consequence. We distinguish four forms of bacteriocin "silence": transcriptional silence, where loci are not detectably expressed under tested conditions; conditional silence, where expression or activity eme
papers.summary: This review argues that while genome and metagenome mining has revealed many predicted bacteriocin loci, sequence data alone cannot establish whether these antimicrobial peptides are actually expressed, deployed, or functionally active in microbial communities. The authors distinguish four forms of bacteriocin 'silence'—transcriptional, conditional, and others—to frame a broader challenge in antimicrobial gene prediction: moving from encoded potential to demonstrated ecological function.

papers.title: Lower 24-hour urinary 6-sulfatoxymelatonin and exploratory bile-acid and microbiome associations in adults with dyslipidemia: a prospectively enrolled cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: We tested the primary hypothesis that lower continuous 24-hour urinary 6-sulfatoxymelatonin (6-SMT) is associated with an adverse lipid and inflammatory profile in adults with dyslipidemia. Associations with FGF19, bile-acid composition, and gut microbiome features were secondary and exploratory.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study examined whether lower 24-hour urinary 6-sulfatoxymelatonin (a melatonin metabolite) is linked to worse lipid and inflammatory profiles in adults with dyslipidemia. Secondary exploratory analyses probed associations with FGF19, bile-acid composition, and gut microbiome features. The findings suggest a potential connection between melatonin levels and metabolic health, though the cross-sectional design limits causal inference.

papers.title: Mapping the knowledge structure and emerging trends of blood-based biomarkers in autism spectrum disorder: A bibliometric analysis (2016-2026).
papers.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a clinically heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition, and its diagnosis still relies mainly on behavioral assessment. Blood-based biomarkers may provide objective support for early detection, biological subgrouping, clinical monitoring, and individualized intervention. However, findings in this field remain dispersed across multiple biological pathways. This study aimed to map the knowledge structure and emerging trends of ASD blood-based biomarker research.
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis maps the knowledge structure and emerging trends in research on blood-based biomarkers for autism spectrum disorder from 2016 to 2026. It synthesizes a dispersed literature spanning multiple biological pathways, aiming to identify research hotspots and future directions for objective diagnostic and subgrouping tools.

papers.title: The chromosomal genome sequence of the staghorn coral, Acropora cervicornis (Lamarck, 1816) (Scleractinia: Acroporidae) and its associated microbial metagenome sequences.
papers.abstract: We present a genome assembly from a specimen of Acropora cervicornis (staghorn coral; Cnidaria; Anthozoa; Scleractinia; Acroporidae). The genome sequence has a total length of 328.68 megabases. Most of the assembly (99.07%) is scaffolded into 14 chromosomal pseudomolecules. The mitochondrial genome has also been assembled, with a length of 18.26 kilobases. Gene annotation of this assembly by Ensembl identified 24,579 protein-coding genes. From the metagenome data, we recovered two bins, of which one was a high-quality MAG.
papers.summary: This paper reports a high-quality chromosome-level genome assembly for the staghorn coral Acropora cervicornis, with 99.07% of the 328.68 Mb sequence scaffolded into 14 chromosomal pseudomolecules and 24,579 protein-coding genes annotated. The authors also assembled the mitochondrial genome and recovered microbial metagenome-assembled genomes, including one high-quality MAG, from associated microbiome data. This resource supports coral genomics, conservation, and reef microbiome research.

papers.title: High-throughput sequencing reveals the virome characteristics of wastewater in Gansu Province, China from 2024 to 2026.
papers.abstract: Emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases continue to pose a persistent challenge to global public health security. As an unbiased and noninvasive population-level surveillance approach, wastewater-based epidemiology has emerged as an urban-scale monitoring tool for proactively capturing the community disease burden. In this study, metagenomic and targeted next-generation sequencing were employed to preliminarily characterize wastewater viral communities in Gansu Province from 2024 to 2026. Across the three annual sampling groups, the Simpson diversity index calculated from metagenomic taxo
papers.summary: This study used metagenomic and targeted next-generation sequencing to characterize viral communities in wastewater samples from Gansu Province, China, collected across 2024–2026. The authors report virome diversity metrics and viral composition across three annual sampling groups, demonstrating the utility of wastewater-based epidemiology for population-level viral surveillance. The work provides a baseline virome profile for the region and supports wastewater monitoring as a proactive public health tool.

papers.title: Altered gut microbial functional landscape in children with pediatric inflammatory multisystem syndrome following SARS-CoV-2 infection: an exploratory metagenomic study.
papers.abstract: Pediatric Inflammatory Multisystem Syndrome (PIMS), also known as MIS-C (Multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children), is a severe post-infectious inflammatory condition associated with SARS-CoV-2 in children. While coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), caused by SARS-CoV-2, primarily affects the respiratory system, growing evidence highlights gastrointestinal involvement and the relevance of the gut-lung axis in systemic inflammation. However, the taxonomic and, particularly, the functional landscape of the gut microbiome in children with PIMS remains insufficiently characterized.
papers.summary: This exploratory metagenomic study characterizes the gut microbiome in children with Pediatric Inflammatory Multisystem Syndrome (PIMS/MIS-C) following SARS-CoV-2 infection, focusing on functional rather than just taxonomic changes. The authors identify altered microbial functional pathways that may contribute to the systemic inflammation seen in PIMS, highlighting the gut-lung axis as a relevant factor. As an exploratory study, it provides a foundation for larger investigations into microbiome-mediated mechanisms in this condition.

papers.title: Cervicovaginal microbiome alterations across HPV infection.
papers.abstract: The cervicovaginal microbiome is a proposed modifier of HPV-associated cervical disease, yet its relationship with viral type heterogeneity, cytological grade, and community state type (CST) remains incompletely understood.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study examines how the cervicovaginal microbiome changes in women with HPV infection, focusing on links between bacterial community state types (CSTs), HPV viral types, and cytological grade. It aims to clarify whether specific microbiome profiles are associated with HPV infection and cervical disease severity.

papers.title: Cross-platform, multi-cohort identification of a caries microbial signature.
papers.abstract: To identify a robust salivary microbial signature associated with caries using a cross-platform, multi-cohort design.
papers.summary: This study uses a cross-platform, multi-cohort design to identify a reproducible salivary microbial signature associated with dental caries. By validating the signature across different sequencing platforms and independent cohorts, the work aims to establish a robust microbial biomarker set for caries risk assessment.

papers.title: Gut microbiota characteristics of gastric cancer patients across distinct pathological stages and their associations with tumor and paratumor mucosal microbiota.
papers.abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) is closely associated with microbial dysbiosis; however, the spatial-temporal characteristics of the gut, paracancerous, and intratumoral microbiomes, as well as their interrelationships during tumor progression, remain insufficiently defined. This study aimed to characterize these microbiomes in 85 GC patients from Northwest China using shotgun metagenomic sequencing and functional annotation. Clinical samples included feces, tumor tissues, and paratumor mucosal tissues (≥5 cm from the tumor margin), enabling comprehensive profiling of microbial composition at the phylum,
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to profile the gut, tumor, and paratumor mucosal microbiomes of 85 gastric cancer patients from Northwest China across different pathological stages. It characterizes microbial composition and functional potential, examining how these distinct microbial niches relate to one another and to tumor progression.

papers.title: Functional organization outweighs spatial separation in structuring microbial communities across a petroleum-hydrocarbon groundwater plume.
papers.abstract: Petroleum-hydrocarbon plumes in groundwater are shaped by hydrological transport, redox conditions, and indigenous microbial activity. However, it remains unclear whether spatial differences among groundwater microbiomes primarily reflect physical separation among wells or ecological reorganization associated with distinct attenuation states within a plume.
papers.summary: This study examines whether microbial community differences across a petroleum-hydrocarbon groundwater plume are driven mainly by physical distance between sampling wells or by ecological reorganization tied to different contaminant-attenuation zones. The authors find that functional organization—the ecological state of the community—outweighs spatial separation in structuring these microbiomes. This suggests that plume biogeochemistry, rather than geography alone, is the primary driver of microbial community composition.

papers.title: Engineering synthetic microbial communities for soil restoration: from rational design to multi-scale biogeochemical applications.
papers.abstract: Soil degradation caused by intensive land use, pollution, and climate stress threatens food production and ecosystem function. Single-strain inoculants often perform inconsistently because they do not persist or compete well in resident soil microbiomes. Synthetic microbial communities (SynComs) combine complementary microbial functions in defined consortia. Their performance, however, depends on community composition and environmental context. Multi-omics, high-throughput screening, and artificial intelligence (AI) can reduce the number of strain combinations that need to be tested. Yet the r
papers.summary: This review argues that synthetic microbial communities (SynComs), which combine complementary microbial functions in defined consortia, can outperform single-strain inoculants for restoring degraded soils. It surveys how multi-omics, high-throughput screening, and AI can guide rational SynCom design and reduce the combinatorial burden of testing strain mixtures, while noting that performance still depends heavily on community composition and environmental context.

papers.title: Omics-based biomarkers of immune-related organ toxicities associated with immune checkpoint inhibitors: a scoping review and evidence map.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) can cause immune-related adverse events (irAEs) across multiple organs. High-throughput omics approaches may help characterize susceptibility, molecular mechanisms, diagnostic features, and monitoring markers related to irAEs; however, evidence remains dispersed across platforms, clinical applications, and toxicity phenotypes.
papers.summary: This scoping review and evidence map consolidates research on omics-based biomarkers for immune-related adverse events (irAEs) caused by immune checkpoint inhibitors across multiple organs. It organizes the dispersed evidence by omics platform, clinical application, and toxicity phenotype, highlighting gaps and opportunities for biomarker development.

papers.title: Metagenomic Tools as Predictive Approaches to Decipher Soil and Rhizosphere Microbial Communities and Their Functions for Sustainable Agriculture.
papers.abstract: The increasing demand for resilient and sustainable food production necessitates a comprehensive understanding of rhizosphere microbial communities and their functional roles in enhancing plant health, nutrient acquisition, stress resilience, and crop productivity, thereby supporting food security and sustainable agriculture. However, soil microbiomes are composed of complex and unculturable communities of beneficial microorganisms that drive critical ecosystem functions, which traditional culture methods cannot capture. This limits the understanding of their roles and impacts on plant health
papers.summary: This review examines how metagenomic tools can predict the composition and functional roles of soil and rhizosphere microbial communities that traditional culture-based methods cannot capture. It argues that these approaches are key to leveraging beneficial microbiomes for plant health, nutrient acquisition, stress resilience, and sustainable crop production.

papers.title: Digital intelligence-enabled tumor microbiome research: from mechanistic dissection to clinical translation.
papers.abstract: Tumor-associated microbiomes are integral components of the tumor microenvironment, modulating tumorigenesis and progression through immune and metabolic pathways. Microbiome data are high-dimensional, sparse, and compositional, which limits conventional analytical approaches. Digital intelligence-an umbrella term encompassing artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), big-data analytics, and multi-omics integration-has emerged as a powerful paradigm for tumor microbiome research. In this review, we delineate the applications of digital intelligence across the full pipeline: intellig
papers.summary: This review describes how artificial intelligence, machine learning, and multi-omics integration are being applied to tumor microbiome research, from mechanistic studies to clinical translation. It highlights how these computational approaches address the high-dimensional, sparse, and compositional nature of microbiome data that limits conventional analysis.

papers.title: Genetic and microbiomics approaches allow the monitoring of the growth of Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus cultures and their environmental influences.
papers.abstract: Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus is cultured in industrial facilities to produce allergen extracts for allergy diagnosis and therapeutic treatment. In these facilities, mite growth and production should be monitored, and exhaustive quality control is mandatory to harvest mites, reach optimal expansion, and avoid potential microbial contamination. In this study, we explored genetic approaches to monitor the growth of five independent D. pteronyssinus cultures. Microbiological studies were performed to characterise the evolution of microbial communities during culture. Finally, we designed a qRT-P
papers.summary: This study used genetic and microbiomic methods to monitor the growth of five independent Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus (house dust mite) cultures in industrial allergen-production facilities. The authors characterized how microbial communities evolved over the course of culturing and developed a qRT-PCR assay to track mite growth. The work provides practical quality-control tools for optimizing mite harvest and detecting microbial contamination in allergen extract production.

papers.title: Spatial multi-omics-guided drug development in inflammatory bowel disease: from mucosal immune niches to precision therapy.
papers.abstract: Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis are now treated with an expanding set of biologics and small molecules, yet treatment selection remains largely empirical. Primary non-response, secondary loss of response, incomplete mucosal healing, fibrostenosis, and fistulizing disease show that conventional clinical, endoscopic, and bulk molecular markers do not capture how disease is organized within tissue. This review argues that the inflamed intestine is better viewed as a set of spatially structured mucosal immune niches rather than as uniform inflammation, with epithelial, myeloid, lymphoid, st
papers.summary: This review argues that inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) should be understood as a collection of spatially organized mucosal immune niches rather than uniform inflammation, and that spatial multi-omics can reveal these niches to guide more precise drug development and therapy selection. It highlights how current clinical, endoscopic, and bulk molecular markers fail to capture tissue-level disease organization, contributing to treatment non-response and complications like fibrostenosis.

papers.title: Integrated Multi-Omics, Machine Learning, and Single-Cell Analysis Provide Insights into Potential Multi-Target Candidate Mechanisms of Combined MAGL11 and Icaritin in Alleviating Imidazole Propionate-Driven Metabolic Intestinal Injury.
papers.abstract: Unhealthy diets, especially high red meat intake, induce gut dysbiosis and abnormal accumulation of a harmful histidine metabolite imidazole propionate (IMP), thereby promoting ulcerative colitis (UC) development. Although combined treatment with a MAGL inhibitor (MAGL11) and icaritin (Y003) exerts combined therapeutic effects in the classical DSS‑induced UC model, its protective effects and molecular mechanisms against IMP‑driven metabolic model remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether combining a MAGL inhibitor (MAGL11) with icaritin can protect against intestinal injury caused by imidazole propionate, a harmful metabolite produced by gut bacteria after high red meat consumption. Using multi-omics, machine learning, and single-cell analysis, the authors identify potential multi-target mechanisms underlying the combined treatment's protective effects in a metabolic model of ulcerative colitis.

papers.title: Correlation analysis between tongue hyperspectral imaging and tongue coating microbiota and feasibility study for early screening of type 2 diabetes mellitus status.
papers.abstract: To investigate the feasibility of applying hyperspectral imaging technology combined with machine learning algorithms for early non-invasive screening of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).
papers.summary: This study explores whether hyperspectral imaging of the tongue, combined with machine learning, can non-invasively screen for type 2 diabetes. The authors correlate tongue imaging features with tongue coating microbiota, suggesting a potential link between spectral signatures and microbial composition. The work is a feasibility study, so results are preliminary and require validation in larger cohorts.

papers.title: Tryptophan metabolism: a critical bridge linking gut microbiota to depression.
papers.abstract: Depression is a major global public health challenge with limitations in current therapies. Emerging evidence highlights that gut microbiota (GM) critically regulates the gut-brain axis via tryptophan (Trp) metabolism. Trp is metabolized through host-directed serotonin (5-HT) and kynurenine (KYN) pathways, as well as microbiota-specific indole derivative pathways. In depression, gut dysbiosis shifts Trp metabolism toward the KYN pathway, leading to accumulation of neurotoxic metabolites such as quinolinic acid and reduced 5-HT synthesis. Microbiota-derived indoles, functioning as key aryl hydr
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence that gut microbiota regulate the gut-brain axis through tryptophan metabolism, with dysbiosis in depression shifting tryptophan toward the neurotoxic kynurenine pathway and away from serotonin synthesis. Microbiota-derived indole derivatives are highlighted as key signaling molecules linking microbial composition to depressive pathology. The authors propose this metabolic crosstalk as a mechanistic bridge and potential therapeutic target for depression.

papers.title: Gut microbiota signatures in mild cognitive impairment: a scoping review of microbial taxa and clinical implications.
papers.abstract: To identify systematically the typical gut microbiota in mild cognitive impairment patients and its association in disease progression. Systematically identify microbial taxa consistently associated with Mild Cognitive Impairment.
papers.summary: This scoping review systematically compiles studies on gut microbiota composition in patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI), identifying microbial taxa that are consistently altered compared to healthy controls. It highlights associations between specific gut bacteria and MCI progression, suggesting potential clinical implications for diagnosis or intervention. The review underscores the need for standardized methodologies to validate these microbial signatures.

papers.title: NeighborFinder: an R package inferring local microbial network around a species of interest.
papers.abstract: Understanding interactions from microbiome data is a central aspect in microbial ecology, as it provides insights into ecosystem stability, disease mechanisms, and can be used to design synthetic communities. Current network inference tools reconstruct global networks from co-abundance data, which means they capture the overall correlation structure for the entire set of taxa considered. These approaches are computationally intensive and suboptimal when the focus is on the local neighborhood of one or a few taxa of interest.
papers.summary: NeighborFinder is an R package that infers the local microbial interaction network surrounding a species of interest, rather than reconstructing a full global co-abundance network. This targeted approach is computationally lighter and better suited for studies focused on one or a few taxa, with applications in microbial ecology, disease research, and synthetic community design.

papers.title: Crotoxin from Crotalus durissus terrificus impairs the establishment of chemically induced colitis in mice associated with formyl peptide receptor signaling.
papers.abstract: Inflammatory bowel diseases (IBDs) arise from a breakdown in tolerance to intestinal microbiota and are characterized by exacerbated inflammatory responses. Epithelial cells of the gastrointestinal tract play a central role in maintaining barrier integrity and orchestrating immune responses; however, the mechanisms underlying epithelial dysfunction and uncontrolled inflammation remain incompletely understood. Crotoxin (CTX), the main component of Crotalus d. terrificus venom, exhibits immunomodulatory activity, making it a promising tool to investigate epithelial-immune interactions in intesti
papers.summary: This study shows that crotoxin, a component of rattlesnake venom, can prevent the development of chemically induced colitis in mice. The protective effect appears to work through formyl peptide receptor signaling, suggesting a role for this pathway in intestinal inflammation. The findings highlight crotoxin as a potential tool for studying epithelial-immune interactions in inflammatory bowel disease.

papers.title: Interpretable machine learning uncovers core seminal microbial signatures in idiopathic oligoasthenospermia.
papers.abstract: Previous studies have confirmed that changes in semen microbiota are closely related to male oligoasthenospermia(OA). However, current research only qualitatively describes the differences in the microbial community, fails to screen out core markers with independent discriminatory value, and also fails to quantitatively evaluate the diagnostic efficacy of the microbial community, resulting in insufficient research on the diagnostic value of the semen microbiota in oligoasthenospermia.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study applies interpretable machine learning to semen microbiome data to identify core microbial signatures that distinguish idiopathic oligoasthenospermia from healthy controls. It moves beyond qualitative descriptions by screening for markers with independent discriminatory value and quantitatively assessing diagnostic efficacy. The work suggests that specific seminal microbes could serve as diagnostic biomarkers for this form of male infertility.
